title: When the Detention Falls
premise: Kestrel Blackwood has spent five years keeping her head down in the small town of Marrow's Bend, channeling everything she can't say into the bread she bakes at her family's bakery. When her grandmother dies and leaves her a recipe box, Kestrel discovers that some 'recipes' are coded instructions—her grandmother was part of a secret network that delivered justice to people the law failed, and Kestrel is now its reluctant heir. As she follows the final unfinished recipe, she uncovers evidence implicating the beloved family of her best friend Wren in a decades-old cover-up, forcing her to choose between loyalty and truth. In the end, Kestrel exposes the truth publicly, losing Wren but gaining a new understanding of justice as something baked by hand, shared openly—and she rewrites the recipe box so the next heir won't have to carry it alone.
about_author: Rosalind Sterling is a former small-town baker who swears her sourdough starter is older than most of her plot twists. She writes stories about quiet kids who discover that silence is also a choice with consequences.

chapters.title: The Weight of Flour
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Morning at Blackwood Bakery: we learn she bakes her feelings—grief bread, apology rolls—and that five years ago something happened that made her vow invisibility. Emotional beat: careful, controlled loneliness.

chapters.title: Grandma June's Last Loaf
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Grandma June dies peacefully; at the funeral everyone praises her pies, but she leaves Kestrel only a battered tin recipe box. Beat: grief mixed with feeling overlooked even in inheritance.

chapters.title: Cardamom and Ciphers
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Sorting the box, Kestrel finds cards that aren't recipes: measurements that don't work, directions like 'fold in the sheriff's Tuesday.' She realizes they're code. Beat: eerie fascination.

chapters.title: Wren Knows Everything Except This
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Best friend Wren Hale jokes through the funeral reception, hiding tension with her golden-boy family, the Ashfords. Beat: loyal warmth laced with secrets on both sides.

chapters.title: The First Instruction
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Deciphering one card leads her to a hollow fence post containing cash and a name: a widow the town failed. Beat: fear curdling into purpose.

chapters.title: Bread for the Widow Okafor
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel anonymously delivers money and bread, watching Mrs. Okafor weep with relief. Beat: first taste of justice outside the law—intoxicating and terrifying.

chapters.title: Five Years Ago
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV (flashback). The accident, the lie Kestrel told to protect someone, and why she stopped speaking up. Beat: shame revealed, stakes established.

chapters.title: The Box Has Rules
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A card addressed 'To whoever inherits' warns: finish the last recipe or the network's records surface and hurt innocents. Beat: inheritance becomes obligation.

chapters.title: Ashford House Smells Like Vanilla
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Dinner at the Ashfords'; Wren notices her father burning papers and her mother's too-bright smile. Beat: dread seeded in the reader before Kestrel knows.

chapters.title: Fold in the Sheriff
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A recipe references Sheriff Dunmore taking payments; Kestrel cross-checks dates against old newspapers in the library. Beat: detective thrill, rising unease.

chapters.title: Someone Else Uses the Oven
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Evidence someone searched the recipe box; flour disturbed, cards reordered. Someone else knows. Beat: paranoia arrives.

chapters.title: The Network Was Never One Person
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Following clues, she finds marks left by past 'bakers'—decades of quiet interventions. Grandma June was a node, not the whole. Beat: awe and scale.

chapters.title: Wren Asks What's Wrong
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Wren senses Kestrel pulling away; Kestrel almost tells her, then lies about a school project. Beat: the friendship's first hairline crack.

chapters.title: Recipe Seven: The Fire
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. An old card describes the mill fire of 1999—the night the Ashford fortune was secured and a night watchman, Elias Crane, died. Beat: history turns sinister.

chapters.title: Elias Crane Had a Daughter
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. She tracks down Crane's daughter, now a tired nurse, who says the town called it an accident and her family broke apart. Beat: abstract injustice gains a human face.

chapters.title: The Sheriff Remembers Me
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Dunmore stops Kestrel outside the library, friendly but pointed: 'Your grandma kept her nose in the oven.' Beat: open threat wrapped in courtesy.

chapters.title: Loyalty Tastes Like Burnt Sugar
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren defends her father to classmates spreading rumors; privately she recalls finding a locked ledger as a child. Beat: denial straining.

chapters.title: The Ledger in the Wall
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A recipe card maps to the old mill; inside, Kestrel finds the Ashford payment ledger proving bribes and the cover-up—with Wren's father's signature. Beat: gut-punch discovery.

chapters.title: What Grandma Knew
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A hidden letter from June explains she gathered proof but died before acting, trusting Kestrel because 'you bake truth into things.' Beat: burden transforms into trust.

chapters.title: Almost Confession
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. On the water tower, Kestrel nearly tells Wren everything; Wren, defensive about her family, snaps. Both leave wounded. Beat: midpoint rupture.

chapters.title: The Bakery Gets a Visitor
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Mr. Ashford visits, buys bread, and mentions how fragile small businesses are—leaving a business card. Beat: menace in politeness; stakes become personal.

chapters.title: Copy Everything
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel photographs the ledger and hides duplicates—in flour tins, in a hymnal—learning tradecraft from June's notes. Beat: resolve hardening into competence.

chapters.title: Dunmore Searches the Shop
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. A 'health inspection' ransacks the bakery; the original ledger vanishes. Kestrel realizes the copies are all that remain. Beat: loss and escalation.

chapters.title: Wren Finds a Photograph
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren discovers her father with Elias Crane the week of the fire and confronts him; he calls it 'complicated.' Beat: Wren's world tilting.

chapters.title: Two Girls, One Truth
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Wren, shaken, comes to the bakery; Kestrel, cornered by Dunmore's surveillance, shows her the copied ledger. Beat: devastating honesty—loyalty vs. truth made flesh.

chapters.title: Wren Chooses
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren walks out without a word, and Kestrel assumes the worst. Beat: heartbreak; the cost of truth arrives early.

chapters.title: The Recipe That Isn't Finished
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The final card is incomplete: 'Deliver the truth where the whole town must taste it,' missing the method. Beat: puzzle pressure; time running out.

chapters.title: Ashford Moves First
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The Ashfords announce a charitable foundation 'honoring the mill workers,' pre-emptively rewriting history; Dunmore threatens Kestrel's parents' lease. Beat: antagonist strikes, clock tightens.

chapters.title: Mrs. Okafor Sees the Ledger
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel shows the nurse the proof; instead of despair, she offers testimony—and reveals others wronged by Ashford over the years. Beat: allies gather; Kestrel no longer alone.

chapters.title: What Wren Did All Night
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Wren confronts her mother, learns her mother knew and stayed silent for the children's sake. Wren photographs her father's private safe combination. Beat: Wren chooses truth at terrible cost.

chapters.title: The Missing Ingredient
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel decodes the final line using June's oldest card: the truth must be delivered publicly, at the foundation's launch—'let them eat it together.' Beat: plan crystallizes.

chapters.title: Baking for Three Hundred
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. All-night bake: Kestrel prints the ledger pages as edible-image transfers on commemorative rolls for the launch. Beat: determined, tender, absurdly brave.

chapters.title: Wren Returns
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Wren brings the safe's contents—originals, including a confession letter her grandfather wrote. Reconciliation, bruised but real. Beat: loyalty realigned with truth.

chapters.title: The Launch
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The town gathers; Ashford speaks of legacy. Kestrel steps forward with the trays. Beat: held breath; point of no return.

chapters.title: Let Them Taste It
chapters.summary: Multiple POVs. The crowd reads the documents on the rolls; murmurs become outrage; Dunmore tries to seize Kestrel, but witnesses—including the nurse—step between. Beat: climax; chaos and catharsis.

chapters.title: Ashford Breaks
chapters.summary: Wren's POV. Confronted publicly and by his own daughter's testimony, Ashford confesses to the fire's cover-up. Wren stands beside Kestrel, not her father. Beat: the fall of the untouchable.

chapters.title: Aftermath in Crumbs
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Investigations begin; the bakery's lease is saved by townsfolk who buy out every tray daily. Some neighbors shun Kestrel still. Beat: bittersweet cost acknowledged.

chapters.title: What We Owe Each Other
chapters.summary: Alternating POVs. Kestrel and Wren repair the friendship slowly, honestly; Kestrel admits her own five-year-old lie and makes amends for it too. Beat: truth applied inward, not just outward.

chapters.title: Rewriting the Recipe Box
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Kestrel adds new cards—not secret instructions, but an open letter: justice should never need to hide again. She keeps one recipe blank. Beat: transformation of inheritance into choice.

chapters.title: Morning Bread
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Months later: sunrise baking, Wren at the counter, the town changed and imperfect. Kestrel bakes a loaf simply called 'Enough.' Beat: warm resolution—visible, unafraid, home.
